page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-8 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains zero local storage disks and no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Instruction set features for the AMD processor include hardware acceleration for cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside advanced vector calculations supported by AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Benchmark assessments show strong single-core stress-ng performance (top 25% at 2865.08) and strong Geekbench text processing (2476.0). Standard multi-core calculations register firmly in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 13500.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7074.0.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate notable divergence between cache and unbuffered operations. Cached read tests reach 566.03 GB/sec, placing it in the average tier. However, large unbuffered block access yields 24.73 GB/sec for reads and 12.1 GB/sec for writes, falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. This bottleneck limits operations that continuously cycle massive, uncached working sets through main memory.

Application benchmarks reflect steady throughput across typical server operations, sustaining 10.82 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 11.11 GB/sec on static web serving. Small-scale model inference achieves 926.93 prompt tokens per second and 229.92 generation tokens per second, though throughput tapers on medium models. The high memory ratio makes the instance suited for in-memory caching layers, medium databases, Clang compilation pipelines, and memory-heavy web applications that rely on persistent network storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-8 is a high-memory general-purpose instance featuring an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor with 8 vCPUs (4 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and dedicated GPUs, it relies on network-attached storage and standard CPU instruction sets including AVX-512 and VAES. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core processing capabilities and competitive Geekbench text processing results, alongside balanced multi-core execution. While cached memory bandwidth performs well at 566.03 GB/sec, large uncached read and write bandwidth is significantly constrained. Redis operations maintain a rate of 10.82 million operations per second, matching expected general-purpose performance. The 8 GB RAM per vCPU allocation positions this server well for memory-bound tasks such as in-memory caches, software compilation, and moderate database workloads.
